- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits mean reversion bias — if recent 7-day average is >70.5, forecast should not exceed 72.0; if <70.0, do not drop below 68.5.
